scenes.vo_text: Take the number itself. Seventy-five million dollars. For a nation of four million farmers, that debt was absurd. There was no central bank. No standing tax system. Just thirteen state treasuries that couldn't agree.

scenes.vo_text: So here's the pattern. America got rich by inventing machines — financial ones, industrial ones, digital ones. Every machine worked. Every machine broke. And the people who ran them usually needed a depression, a war, or a panic to admit the old machine was done.

scenes.vo_text: The country hit twenty-seven trillion dollars in annual output not because it avoided breaking — but because it rebuilt faster than it fell. Each rebuild moved the bill somewhere else: onto workers, taxpayers, debtors, or the next generation. Growth made the balance sheet larger. It never made the balance sheet disappear.
